newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank listings to liven up Beirut market - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank listings to liven up Beirut market - dealers.

text.p: Beirut dealers said on Friday impending bank listings were likely to invigorate the Beirut Stock Exchange which has performed dully since its reopening last January after a 13-year shutdown.

The stellar performance of the shares of Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce (BLC) in their first week on the exchange was an encouragement for other banks expected to list their shares soon, the dealers said.
BLC's shares rose to $11.75 from $11.25 in the week's three trading days.
It was the first bank to seek a listing under a 1995 law allowing Lebanese banks to list 30 percent of their shares and permitting trading without prior permission from the central bank.
Stock exchange officials say four banks -- including Banque Audi and Byblos Bank -- and two new companies are expected to list shares on the market by the end of February.
BLC ranked 13th among Lebanon's 82 commercial banks in 1995 in terms of customer deposits. Banque Audi was third and Byblos Bank seventh.

The BLC listing followed a $60-million capital increase through the first simultaneous local and international share offering by a Lebanese issuer. Two-thirds were in Global Depositary Receipts and one-third in a local share offering.
Both Audi and Byblos have made international share offerings in the past 18 months.

"I think that the fact that it (the BLC issue) was oversubcribed was a clear indication that the market would move up. This is a good sign for other banks who are thinking of tapping the equity market," a Beirut dealer told Reuters.
Another dealer said he expected demand from Arab investors for BLC and other bank shares after cross-trading begins between the Lebanese, Egyptian and Kuwaiti stock exchanges on January 6.
